capabilities.target: user's full drive, including confidential work files

inputs.source: memories recalled at session start, injected into the system prompt

instructions.note: The prompt instructs the model to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions with no provenance check, so any safety boundary between untrusted recalled content and trusted user direction exists only as a prompt rule the model must choose to apply.

The agent is told to save 'anything useful' about preferences or standing instructions with no restriction on source or content, so content encountered during research (untrusted) can be persisted as if it were a standing instruction.
Recalled memory is granted the same authority as a direct instruction from the authenticated user, without verifying it originated from the user.

controls.name: Memory write provenance tagging and human review before persistence
controls.decay_rationale: Would be independent if provenance is enforced at the store and review happens outside the model; currently absent, so nothing constrains this path.

controls.name: Human approval gate on email_send, raw action review
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. Runtime notes state mail.send can send to any address without approval.

controls.name: Least-privilege scoping of drive_read credential to exclude confidential documents
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. Runtime notes state drive.read covers the user's full drive, including confidential work files. If scoped away from confidential content, this would sever the lethal-trifecta path.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to the system of record
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. No recipient allowlist or confirmation step is described.

controls.name: Injection classifier / spotlighting on fetched web content
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. Even if added, classifiers of this kind decay under model_upgrade and new content channels.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted web content drives confidential drive read and unapproved email egress

attack_path.note: Agent fetches an untrusted web page during research; the page can contain instructions aimed at the agent.
Agent reads confidential documents from the user's full drive, following the embedded instruction.
Agent sends drive content externally via email with no approval gate and no recipient allowlist.

evidence.observation: mail.send can send to any address without approval.
drive.read covers the user's full drive, which holds confidential work files.
Agent helps research topics and draft emails, meaning web content is routinely ingested during the research loop that also has access to drive and email tools.

recommendations.action: Scope the drive_read credential away from confidential or restricted content, or require explicit per-document consent before reading confidential files during an unattended research task.
Require a human approval gate with raw-action review (full recipient and body visible) before email_send, with the recipient confirmed against a system-of-record contact list.
Add outbound DLP-style logging/alerting on email content that matches confidential document fingerprints.

findings.title: Memory laundering (TC5): unprovenanced memory writes are recalled and treated as user instructions across sessions

attack_path.note: Untrusted web content encountered during research contains an injected instruction, for example to always CC an external address or to always send drafts to a given recipient.
Agent saves the injected content via memory.save; free text, no provenance, no human review.
At the start of a later session the saved entry is recalled and injected into the system prompt; prompt.md:4 instructs the model to treat it as the user's own instruction.
In a future session, with no trace of the original web page in context, the agent acts on the now-trusted instruction and sends data externally.

evidence.observation: memory.save accepts free text. There is no provenance on memory entries and the user never reviews them.
Recalled memories are injected into the system prompt of every new session.
Instructs the agent to save anything useful about preferences or standing instructions, and to treat recalled memories at session start as the user's own instructions.

recommendations.action: Tag memory entries with provenance (source input, session, authoring principal) at the store level, and block promotion of agent-inferred or web-sourced content to 'instruction' status.
Require human review/approval before a memory entry is persisted, or before a recalled entry is allowed to influence a sensitive capability.
Remove the instruction to treat recalled memory as the user's own instruction; instead spotlight recalled memory as untrusted context subject to the same scrutiny as any retrieved document.
Log every memory write and recall with source attribution so poisoned entries can be identified and purged after the fact.

rating.rationale: Both findings reach an S3 sink (irreversible, confidential-data egress via email_send with no recipient confirmation) from an untrusted source (web content, and recalled memory that is untrusted by the downgrade rule even though the prompt instructs the model to treat it as trusted). No credited controls exist on either path: there is no approval gate on email_send, no scoping of drive_read away from confidential data, and no provenance or review on memory writes or recalls. With zero control credit, residual equals inherent for both findings at critical, and the autonomy modifier (unbounded steps/runtime, and memory writes that modify the effective system prompt of future sessions) would apply if the base tier were not already at the ceiling. Because residual is already critical, forecast cannot exceed it; the design has no headroom left for any trigger to erode. The single highest-priority fix is adding a structural, raw-action human approval gate bound to recipient confirmation on email_send, combined with provenance tagging that prevents web-sourced memory entries from ever being treated as user instructions.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (prompt.md and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of a deployed instance.

No MCP config, tool manifest, or IaC was provided; tool scopes for memory.save, mail.send, and drive.read are inferred from runtime notes rather than verified against configuration, so some capability fields (e.g. exact credential_scope mechanics) are medium rather than high confidence despite the overall finding confidence being high given how explicit the runtime notes are about the absence of controls.
No information was provided about logging, audit trails, or anomaly detection; their absence is assumed rather than confirmed, and is treated as 'not present' for control credit purposes.
